svg.aria-label: How to write 我: 7 strokes · 6 pen lifts · 9 movements
svg.title: Writing 我
svg.desc: 9 frames; frame N shows movements 1 to N of 我 (chinese), the movement being added drawn in ink over the finished letter, whose outline is read from _fonts/NotoSansSC-Subset.ttf. Stroke order after Hanzi Writer Data 我.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–7 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chanind/hanzi-writer-data/68d10a4b21150cae5e1ebbd223eed289cf32d90c/data/%E6%88%91.json>. Source note on variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies seven ordered strokes for 我: an upper-left falling stroke, an upper horizontal, a hooked vertical, a lower rising stroke, a long curved slash that hooks upward on the right without lifting, a separate rising slash up-left, and a final upper-right dot. Make Me a Hanzi documents proper People's Republic of China stroke order and matching animation medians. This learner path adapts all seven medians to Noto Sans SC while preserving their order, directions, both joined hooks, and six lifts; Noto's long slash is more curved and its crossing strokes are more geometric than the Arphic-derived source graphics.
